en.name: Roasted red peppers, jarred
en.summary: Jarred roasted red peppers keep 4–6 months in the refrigerator. They are packed in an acidified brine, which is what makes that long refrigerated life possible — but only while the peppers stay under the liquid and the jar stays cold.
en.pantry: An unopened jar sits in a cool, dark, dry cupboard until its printed date; that shelf life comes from the heat processing, the acid in the packing liquid and the intact vacuum seal, not from the peppers. Check the lid before you open one: it should be concave and should pop when first opened. A jar with a domed or bulging lid, a broken seal, leakage around the rim, or liquid that spurts out goes in the bin unopened and untasted. Once the jar is open it stops being a cupboard item entirely.
en.fridge: Refrigerated at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, roasted red peppers keep 4–6 months — a long window by the standards of an opened jar, and it is the acidity of the brine that earns it. Two conditions attach. Keep the peppers fully submerged in their liquid; any piece standing proud of the surface will grow mould first. And use a clean fork every time, because a used one introduces exactly the contamination the acid was holding off. If you top the jar up, use the brine it came in rather than water or oil.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is published for jarred roasted peppers, and the texture is the problem rather than the safety: pepper flesh is largely water and already soft from roasting, so ice crystals collapse it and it thaws limp and weeping. That is acceptable in a sauce, a soup or a romesco, not on a plate. If you freeze them, drain them first, portion them flat, and plan to use them in something blended or cooked.
en.thawing: Thaw in the fridge and use in a cooked or blended dish. Expect the peppers to be limp and to release water, and do not refreeze them.
spoilage: A bulging or domed lid, a jar that leaks, or brine that spurts when opened.
Mould at the surface, usually on a piece that was above the liquid.
Peppers that have turned slimy, or a sour, yeasty smell instead of a sweet smoky one.
tips: Keep the peppers pushed down under the brine after every use.
Use a clean fork, never fingers or a used utensil.
Write the opening date on the lid — 4–6 months is long enough to forget.
Save the brine; it is useful in dressings and keeps the peppers covered.

faq.q: How long do jarred roasted peppers keep after opening?
faq.a: 4–6 months refrigerated at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, as long as they stay submerged in their brine.

faq.q: Do roasted peppers in a jar need to be refrigerated?
faq.a: An unopened jar does not — keep it in a cool dark cupboard to its printed date. Once opened, it must be refrigerated.

faq.q: Can you freeze jarred roasted peppers?
faq.a: No timeline is published and the texture collapses. Drain and freeze them only for sauces, soups or purées.

zh.name: 瓶裝烤紅椒
zh.summary: 瓶裝烤紅椒冷藏可放 4～6 個月。它泡在加了酸的醃汁裡，那正是它冷藏後還能撐這麼久的原因——但前提是紅椒始終浸在液面下、而且全程保持低溫。
zh.pantry: 未開封的玻璃罐放陰涼、避光、乾燥的櫥櫃，用到包裝上印的日期為止；那個常溫壽命來自加熱殺菌、醃汁的酸度與完好的真空密封，不是來自紅椒本身。開罐前先看蓋子：它應該是微凹的，第一次旋開時會「啵」一聲。蓋子鼓起、密封失效、罐口滲漏，或開罐時汁液噴出來的，不要打開、不要試吃，直接丟棄。罐子一開，它就完全不再是櫥櫃食品。
zh.fridge: 冷藏在 4 °C 以下，烤紅椒可放 4～6 個月——以「開過的罐子」而言算很長，而這段時間是醃汁的酸度掙來的。但它附帶兩個條件：第一，紅椒一定要完全浸在汁液裡，任何露出液面的那一片都會最先長霉；第二，每次都要用乾淨的叉子，因為用過的叉子帶進去的，正是那些酸度原本擋住的東西。要補液體的話，請用原本的醃汁，不要加水或加油。
zh.freezer: 瓶裝烤紅椒沒有公布的冷凍期限，而問題出在質地而不是安全：甜椒果肉幾乎都是水，烤過之後又已經很軟，冰晶會把它撐垮，解凍後軟塌又出水。這用在醬汁、湯或 romesco 裡可以接受，直接擺盤就不行。要冷凍請先瀝乾、攤平分裝，並且規劃用在打碎或燉煮的料理上。
zh.thawing: 放冷藏解凍，用在需要加熱或打碎的料理。要有軟塌出水的心理準備，也不要再次冷凍。
spoilage: 蓋子鼓起、罐子滲漏，或開罐時醃汁噴出。
醃汁變混濁、牽絲或冒泡。
表面長霉，通常長在露出液面的那一片上。
紅椒變黏滑，或聞起來發酸、有酵母味，而不是甜香帶煙燻味。
tips: 每次用完都把紅椒壓回汁液下面。
用乾淨的叉子，不要用手或用過的餐具。
在蓋子上寫開罐日期，4～6 個月長到足以讓人忘記。
醃汁別倒掉，做油醋很好用，也是讓紅椒保持浸沒的關鍵。

faq.q: 瓶裝烤紅椒開封後可以放多久？
faq.a: 冷藏 4 °C 以下 4～6 個月，前提是紅椒一直浸在醃汁裡。

faq.q: 瓶裝烤紅椒需要冷藏嗎？
faq.a: 未開封不用，放陰涼暗處、依包裝日期使用即可。一旦開封就必須冷藏。

faq.q: 瓶裝烤紅椒可以冷凍嗎？
faq.a: 沒有公布的期限，而且質地會塌掉。要冷凍請先瀝乾，並且只用在醬汁、湯或打碎的料理。
